titlePl: Ósmoklasista: Praca — 36 haseł do gier LingoSpark
titleEn: Grade 8 English: Work & Jobs — 36 terms for LingoSpark games
blurbPl: Dział Praca na ósmoklasistę: zawody, etat, rozmowa kwalifikacyjna. Prostsze niż matura — pod gry LingoSpark.
blurbEn: Grade-8 Work module: job names, hours, interviews. Simpler than Matura — built for LingoSpark games.

items.definitionEn: a person whose job is to stop fires
items.example: A firefighter has a dangerous but important job.

items.definitionEn: a person who looks after patients in hospital
items.example: My mother is a nurse at the local hospital.

items.definitionEn: a person who repairs cars or machines
items.example: The mechanic is repairing my dad's car today.

items.definitionEn: a person who helps customers in a shop
items.example: The shop assistant was polite and helpful.

items.definitionEn: a person who brings food to tables in a restaurant
items.example: The waiter brought our pizza to the table.

items.definitionEn: a person who writes news for papers or websites
items.example: She is a journalist and writes articles every week.

items.definitionEn: a person who designs machines, roads or software
items.example: My father works as an engineer in a big company.

items.definitionEn: a person who advises people about the law
items.example: You should talk to a lawyer before you sign the contract.

items.definitionEn: a skilled cook who runs a restaurant kitchen
items.example: A chef works in the kitchen of a restaurant.

items.definitionEn: a person who repairs water pipes and taps
items.example: Call a plumber if the tap will not stop dripping.

items.definitionEn: a person whose job is to make sure people follow the law
items.example: The police officer helped the lost tourist.

items.definitionEn: a person who writes computer programs
items.example: He would like to work as a computer programmer.

items.definitionEn: to formally ask for a job
items.example: She wants to apply for a summer job in a café.

items.definitionEn: a meeting where you answer questions about a job
items.example: Wear something smart for the interview.

items.definitionEn: a document with your education and work history
items.example: Write a short CV even if you have only helped at home.

items.definitionEn: money you receive every month for your job
items.example: The salary is paid at the end of the month.

items.definitionEn: without a paid job
items.example: He has been unemployed since the shop closed.

items.definitionEn: working fewer hours than a full week
items.example: He has a part-time job in a café after school.

items.definitionEn: working the complete normal number of hours
items.example: After school she wants a full-time job.

items.definitionEn: extra hours after normal work time
items.example: Mum did overtime last week to finish a report.

items.definitionEn: a period of work, for example morning or night
items.example: Nurses often work a night shift.

items.definitionEn: a person or company that pays people to work
items.example: A good employer trains new staff.

items.definitionEn: a person who is paid to work for a company
items.example: Every employee must wear a name badge.

items.definitionEn: a person you work with
items.example: Ask a colleague if you do not understand the task.

items.definitionEn: giving a lot of money for the work
items.example: IT jobs are often well-paid but stressful.

items.definitionEn: causing a lot of worry or pressure
items.example: Working in an emergency room is stressful.

items.definitionEn: to do your job in your house, not in an office
items.example: Dad can work from home on Fridays.

items.definitionEn: to stop working, usually because of age
items.example: Grandad will retire next year.

items.definitionEn: things you can do well because of practice or training
items.example: Teamwork is one of the most useful skills.

items.definitionEn: knowledge you get by doing a job
items.example: Babysitting counts as work experience.

items.definitionEn: a typical full-time office day
items.example: She does not want a nine-to-five office job.

items.definitionEn: a job that is available
items.example: There is a vacancy for a shop assistant in the mall.

items.definitionEn: to be given paid work
items.example: He hopes to get a job in a sports shop.

items.definitionEn: to receive money for work you do
items.example: How much do waiters earn in the summer?

items.definitionEn: to have as your job
items.example: What does your brother do for a living?

items.definitionEn: working for yourself, not for a boss
items.example: Many hairdressers are self-employed.
